extracted.intended_audience: federal agency staff responsible for tribal consultation and Tribal governments/authorized representatives who submit tribal comments
extracted.subtask_description: Uniform standards for government-to-government tribal consultation and guidance for effective Tribal comments on federal actions with Tribal implications. Covers notice timing, definition, outcomes disclosure, recordkeeping, and recommended content and framing for Tribal submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and Time
rubrics_metrics.description: 30 days' notice of consultation is the standard; when time constraints prevent 30 days' notice, the notice should explain why; upon a tribe's request, agencies should consider adjusting deadlines for notice and for accepting written comments; when practicable, a comment period of 60 to 120 days will be provided, to allow sufficient time for Tribal Officials to consult with their members and legal counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide at least 30 days' advance notice; if providing less, explain the time constraint in the notice. Be prepared to adjust deadlines if a Tribe requests it. Aim for a written comment period of 60–120 days when practicable to allow government-to-government coordination and internal Tribal deliberation and legal review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Tribal Consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribal Consultation involves the direct, timely, and interactive process of receiving input from Indian Tribes regarding proposed Treasury actions on Policies that have Tribal Implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame consultation as a government-to-government interactive process (not a one-way notice or a generic solicitation of public comment). Ensure mechanisms allow direct, timely, and two-way engagement with Tribal officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The head of each agency shall timely disclose to the affected Tribe or Tribes the outcome of the consultation and decisions made as a result of the consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After consultation concludes, promptly communicate decision outcomes to Tribes, including whether and how Tribal input affected final decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability Record
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division shall maintain a consultation record that includes: a summary of the Tribal input received; a general explanation of how the Tribal input received influenced or was incorporated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep an auditable record capturing Tribal input and a narrative explaining how that input was considered and/or integrated into agency decisions—this documents procedural accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify Tribal government and authorized representative
rubrics_metrics.description: For Tribal commenters, effective comments: Identify the Tribal government and authorized representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state the governmental status of the commenter and provide evidence or citation of authorization (e.g., resolution, letter of authorization) so the comment is treated as government-to-government communication rather than an individual submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite Tribal sovereignty principles
rubrics_metrics.description: For Tribal commenters, effective comments: Cite Tribal sovereignty principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly reference tribal sovereignty as a legal and policy foundation for the Tribe's positions, explaining how proposed actions implicate sovereign rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference specific federal trust obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: For Tribal commenters, effective comments: Reference specific federal trust obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the proposed action relates to the federal trust relationship; identify the trust duties at issue and link factual or legal arguments to those obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address the Tribal Implications dimension explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: For Tribal commenters, effective comments: Address the Tribal Implications dimension explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make an explicit showing of how the action has 'Tribal Implications'—describe impacts, affected Tribal interests, and why consultation is warranted under the agency's standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite federal trust statutes (e.g., Indian Self-Determination Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Tribal commenters, effective comments: Cite federal trust statutes (Indian Self-Determination Act, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference relevant statutes and legal authorities by name (and citation where appropriate) to anchor legal claims about obligations and duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide traditional ecological knowledge where relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: For Tribal commenters, effective comments: Provide traditional ecological knowledge where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, include and explain Traditional Ecological Knowledge (TEK) as a substantive, place-based source of information—describe its provenance and relevance to the agency decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address consultation procedural adequacy as well as substance
rubrics_metrics.description: For Tribal commenters, effective comments: Address consultation procedural adequacy as well as substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate both whether the consultation process met procedural expectations (notice, timing, opportunity to be heard, recordkeeping) and whether the substantive concerns raised by the Tribe were adequately considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish government-to-government comments from individual comments
rubrics_metrics.description: For Tribal commenters, effective comments: Distinguish from individual citizen comments through government-to-government framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use government-to-government language and provide evidence of official status so the submission is processed under tribal consultation frameworks rather than generic public-comment channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal consultation is distinct from APA notice-and-comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribal consultation is a separate statutory and policy obligation: EO 13175 (Consultation and Coordination With Indian Tribal Governments); each agency's tribal consultation policy; government-to-government, not stakeholder-to-agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat consultation obligations as independent of—and in addition to—APA notice-and-comment requirements. Follow Executive Orders and each agency's specific tribal consultation policies; do not conflate stakeholder engagement with government-to-government consultation.
